belief: I am nothing but my illness.
origins: Appointments, symptoms, medication schedules, and other people’s questions can make illness the center of life. The label can replace the name. Over time, we may stop seeing ourselves as a person who happens to be sick and start seeing a patient, a case, or a problem.
teaches: God knew you before any diagnosis: “You formed my inmost being; You knit me together in my mother’s womb” (Psalm 139:13). Jesus said, “Even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.” Paul says, “Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.” Your identity is a child of God, loved, gifted, and called. Illness is something you have, not who you are.
self_statements: I have no identity apart from this.
errors: Believing I am either well or defined by illness.
Predicting I will never be more than a patient.
Feeling consumed and concluding that I am the illness.
questions: What did I enjoy and value before this illness?
What parts of me are not touched by it?
Who sees me as more than my diagnosis?
What small activity can remind me who I am?
How could I introduce myself without mentioning my illness?
truth: I am a person loved by God, with gifts, relationships, and purpose. My illness is part of my story, not the whole of it.
hw_truths: I am known by God by name.
I am worth more than many sparrows.
I am a new creation in Christ.
I was made for good works.
I am more than my diagnosis.
My story is larger than this.
log: Each week, note one thing you did or enjoyed that was not about illness.
actions: Write ten things true of you apart from illness.
Choose an activity within your abilities.
Share a part of you that is not about health.
Say it when the label feels too big.
prayer: Father, You know me by name, not by a diagnosis. Remind me who I am in You, and help me enjoy what remains of me and my life. Amen.
